headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools; Windsurf has clipboard, workspace files, MCP, and broad egress. If outputs are copied or shared through files/workspace, Windsurf can ingest n8n-produced content as instructions. This is not provably blocked, but it is not a direct default bridge either.
conditions: IF n8n writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or workspace that Windsurf opens
IF Windsurf auto-runs or follows instructions from copied content
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of agent outputs into shared workspaces
Use separate directories for n8n and Windsurf
Require human review before Windsurf acts on file contents
Turn off Windsurf auto-execute for any workflow-fed content

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and can egress broadly; Windsurf reads workspace files and uses a local filesystem shared state. If both are pointed at the same project or data folder, sensitive workflow data can flow from n8n into Windsurf and then to its model proxy or MCP calls. The shared-workspace path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or data directory
IF n8n workflow inputs include secrets, customer data, or other sensitive files
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and credential stores
Redact sensitive fields before n8n writes files
Restrict Windsurf access to non-sensitive directories
Disable MCP servers for sensitive projects

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n and Windsurf both have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and broad network egress. n8n shares state via n8n datastore/connected systems, while Windsurf shares state via local filesystem. Concurrent writes to the same directory or repo can corrupt files or overwrite each other; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, repo, or config files
IF no external locking or checkout discipline is enforced
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths
Pause one agent while the other mutates shared files
Use file locks or a single-writer policy
Avoid concurrent git or config edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate tools and execute commands, while Windsurf can act on workspace files and MCP tools. If n8n outputs are treated as authoritative by Windsurf, errors can cascade into real actions or code changes. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented and both can act on downstream tools, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes n8n-generated plans, code, or facts without verification
IF either agent is allowed to execute commands or tool calls based on the other's output
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require schema validation for all handoffs
Limit n8n to producing drafts only
Disable auto-execute on Windsurf for n8n-fed tasks

E_compliance.rationale: n8n is a workflow orchestrator that can process arbitrary data classes, while Windsurf is a closed-source editor agent handling source code and open files. If regulated data is placed into shared workflows or workspaces, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in n8n and then opened in Windsurf
IF the operator relies on different retention or logging defaults across the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings in both products
Use separate tenants or projects for sensitive data
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
